blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Accounting is how a company keeps track of its money. Every sale, every bill and every salary is recorded. So, at any moment, the company can answer three simple questions: how much do we earn, how much do we spend, and how much do we really have?

Without accounting, a company is flying blind. With good accounting, leaders can see the truth about the business. Then they can make honest decisions based on it.

Accounting is not just about numbers. It is the language the whole business uses to talk about itself.

items.q: What does accounting do for a company?
options: It keeps track of the company's money
items.why: "Accounting is how a company keeps track of its money."

items.q: What three things are recorded?
options: Every email, meeting and phone call
items.why: "Every sale, every bill and every salary is recorded."

items.q: What three questions can the company answer?
options: How much we earn, spend and really have
How many people, offices and teams
items.why: "how much do we earn, how much do we spend, and how much do we really have?"

items.q: The text says a company without accounting is "flying blind." This suggests that…
options: the company cannot see the truth about its money
the company travels a lot by plane
the company has too many leaders
items.why: Inferência: "flying blind" = voando às cegas, ou seja, sem enxergar a verdade sobre o negócio.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: Accounting helps leaders make honest decisions
Accounting is a language of the business
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz o contrário — "Accounting is not just about numbers."

blocks.instruction: Ouça James falar com o novo estagiário. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome to the team. Let me tell you something important on your first day. Some people think the accounting team just counts money in a back room. That is not true here.

At Czarnikow, we treat accounting as seriously as sales. Why? Because every board meeting starts with our numbers. When the leaders sit down, they want to know one thing: what is the truth about the business? And we give them that answer.

Every day, we record every sale, every bill and every salary. It sounds simple, but it is the foundation of trust. If our numbers are wrong, the leaders make bad decisions. If our numbers are honest, they can act with confidence.

So never think this job is small. You are not just typing numbers. You are helping the whole company see clearly. That is why the accounting team is at every important meeting. Take it seriously, and you will do well here.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Czarnikow treat the accounting team?
items.why: "we treat accounting as seriously as sales."

items.q: What do the leaders want to know at a board meeting?
options: The plan for next year's party
The name of the new intern
items.why: "they want to know one thing: what is the truth about the business?"

items.q: According to James, what happens if the numbers are wrong?
items.why: "If our numbers are wrong, the leaders make bad decisions."

items.q: James says the intern is "not just typing numbers." He suggests that…
options: the work has a bigger purpose
items.why: Inferência: ele mostra que o trabalho ajuda toda a empresa a enxergar com clareza — vai além de digitar números.

items.q: Why is the accounting team at every important meeting?
options: Because it sits near the boardroom
Because it has the biggest team
Because its numbers shape the decisions
items.why: Inferência: as reuniões começam com os números do time, então ele precisa estar presente.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We record every payment in the system." To record means to…
options: write it down and keep it
items.why: To record = registrar, anotar e guardar a informação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The company must pay every ___ on time, or the lights go off."
items.why: Bill = conta a pagar (por exemplo, a conta de luz).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A good business tries to ___ more money than it spends."
items.why: To earn = ganhar dinheiro; o oposto de spend (gastar).

items.q: "We track every cost this month." To track means to…
options: follow it and watch it closely
items.why: To track = acompanhar, seguir de perto.

items.q: "A good leader must be honest with the numbers." Honest means…
items.why: Honest = honesto, que diz a verdade.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples que aparecem em conversas de trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval.

items.q: "Please keep track of your expenses." This means to…
items.why: Keep track of = acompanhar, manter registro.

items.q: "The numbers do not add up." This means they…
items.why: Add up = fazer sentido, bater certo (as contas).

items.q: "Can you write down the total?" To write down means to…
options: note it on paper or screen
items.why: Write down = anotar, registrar por escrito.

items.q: "We need to find out how much we really have." To find out means to…
items.why: Find out = descobrir, obter a informação.
